newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy gov may call five confidence votes on budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy gov may call five confidence votes on budget.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government could call as many as five confidence votes on its 1997 budget to sweep aside a mountain of amendments in the Senate (upper house), Coviello Romualdo, chairman of the Senate budget commission, said Friday.
He said he expected the government to make a confidence issue of four or five articles of the bill to which the opposition has submitted more than 3,000 amendments.
"We will wait until they start filibustering and then (the government) will make it a confidence issue," Romualdo told reporters.
The budget bill has to be approved by the Senate by December 19 according to the parliamentary schedule.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government has said the deadline will be impossible to meet unless the opposition withdraws the bulk of its amendments.
Prodi has a comfortable majority in the Senate and would not risk defeat in a confidence vote.
